version.changelog:
Initial release of Feishu Testcase Writer.

- Converts Feishu/Lark requirement document links into structured, review-ready QA testcase docs in the team's approved style.
- Automatically decomposes modules and business rules into hierarchical testcases, covering list/detail pages, field rules, status flows, calculations, and permissions.
- Discovers available Feishu tools for online doc reading and cloud doc writing; offers fallback to Markdown if tools are unavailable.
- Ensures all testcases include placeholders for evidence and open questions, without fabricating results or data.
- Outputs documents with stable headings, explicit rule breakdowns, clear module separation, and compliance with reviewed document templates.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: feishu-pro-testcase-generation
Version: 1.0.0

The skill is designed to automate the generation of QA test cases from Feishu/Lark requirement documents into new Feishu cloud docs. The instructions in SKILL.md and the reference files (doc-template.md, reviewed-style.md) focus on maintaining a specific hierarchical structure and ensuring testability without fabricating data. While reviewed-style.md references local file paths as examples of approved styles, there is no evidence of intentional data exfiltration, malicious execution, or harmful prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill is an instruction-only helper that reads Feishu/Lark requirement links, drafts structured QA testcases, and (when available) writes them back to Feishu — its requirements and instructions are coherent with that purpose.

dimensions.detail: The name and description (generate Feishu testcases from requirement links and save to a Feishu doc) match the instructions. The skill declares no binaries, env vars, or installs — all consistent for an instruction-only converter that relies on existing Feishu/Lark tooling provided by the agent environment.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md confines runtime actions to: discover available Feishu/Lark tools, fetch the provided online doc link, decompose content into testcases using the supplied templates, and create a Feishu cloud doc. It explicitly forbids fabricating execution results and asks for pasted content only if link access is unavailable. The only minor note is that reference sample text includes local file paths (e.g., /Users/...), but those are template examples and the instructions do not ask to read local files.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files — the skill is instruction-only, so nothing will be downloaded or written to disk by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials. It does expect the agent environment to expose Feishu/Lark read/write tools; if such tools exist they will use whatever credentials are already provisioned by the platform. Confirm that those Feishu/Lark integrations have appropriate scope (read/create docs only) before granting access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (normal). disable-model-invocation:false (normal default). The skill does not request permanent agent-level privileges or try to modify other skills or platform configs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears internally consistent and does only what it claims: read Feishu/Lark links, generate testcases using the included templates, and save to Feishu if a write tool is available. Before installing, verify the following: (1) which Feishu/Lark tool the agent will use — ensure its OAuth/token scope is limited to reading and creating docs (no broad admin rights); (2) whether the agent will write into shared folders or spaces — provide a target folder or restrict write access if needed; (3) if you prefer not to grant doc-write access, run the skill in a mode where it returns Markdown output for manual review and paste-to-Feishu yourself; and (4) the reference files include example local paths but the skill does not attempt to read local files. If the platform exposes any unknown third-party Feishu connector, review that connector's trustworthiness before use.
